claude-sonnet-5.grok-4: Comprehensive, faithful coverage of nearly every chapter with dialogue lifted almost verbatim from the source. Character names and physical tags (Red Sweater, weazened Perrault, swarthy Francois) are consistent. A few scenes stack multiple actions/locations into single headings (e.g. team-formation montage beats), slightly hurting clip-by-clip directibility. Adds one small invented line ('He has earned it') but nothing structurally disruptive. No explicit sound/music cues are given anywhere, only sparse atmosphere.
claude-sonnet-5.grok-4.5: Strong fidelity with an explicit production note locking Buck's visual identity, which helps casting consistency. However it repeatedly leans on 'Montage, tight' scene headings that compress many distinct actions/locations into one block (e.g., the entire Dyea-to-Bennett trek, or the entire wilderness prospecting stretch), which directly conflicts with the single-clip-per-beat directive and lowers directibility/pacing granularity versus more evenly beat-broken scripts. Dialogue is period-accurate and lifted faithfully. No real music/SFX cueing beyond descriptive prose.
claude-sonnet-5.claude-sonnet-5: The most complete and well-organized adaptation: covers every major beat (Curly's death, Spitz feud, Dolly's madness, Hal/Mercedes ordeal, Thornton rescue, the wager, the moose hunt, and the Yeehat massacre/wolf-pack finale) with clear, mostly single-action scene headings that suit short-clip generation. A locked visual-identity note for Buck and distinct descriptors for secondary characters (Hans as 'big placid Scandinavian,' Perrault 'weazened') support consistent casting. Still lacks explicit music/sound cues, relying only on descriptive atmosphere, which caps the sound-design score.
claude-sonnet-5.o3-mini: This is closer to a loose two-page treatment than a full adaptation. It invents named characters not in the book, skips nearly every major event and supporting character, and relies on unfilmable internal-state narration ('embraced his true self,' 'the ties of the past loosened'). Pacing has no real escalation because almost the entire middle of the novel is missing. Not usable as a shootable draft.
claude-sonnet-5.gemini-2.5-flash: Extremely thorough, near line-by-line fidelity to the novel with almost no invented content (aside from the minor spelling 'Billy' vs. 'Billee'). Scene breakdown is granular and mostly single-action, good for clip generation, though some scenes still bundle two or three sequential beats. Dialogue is authentic and well-portioned. Notably, action lines frequently embed capitalized onomatopoeia (CHINKS, GROWLS, WHISTLES, CRACKS, SCREAMS) that double as usable sound-design cues, giving it the strongest (if still modest) sound-design implementation among the set.
claude-sonnet-5.gpt-4o-mini: Covers most major plot points but drops the moose-hunt sequence entirely and adds substantial invented, sentimentalized dialogue ('You're not just my dog, Buck. You're my heart,' 'Adventure awaits!') that is tonally inconsistent with Jack London's harsher period voice. Inconsistent spelling of recurring names (PERRAULT/PERREAULT, SALOON-KEEPER/SALON-KEEPER, YEEHATS/YEHAATS) undermines casting-reference consistency. Several action lines lean on unfilmable internal description ('his spirit rekindled,' 'a spark of wildness igniting within him'). Pacing sags in repetitive, low-content White River Camp scenes before the climax.

gemini-2.5-flash.o3-mini: Screenplay A suffers from severe adaptation fidelity issues, including invented named characters and the complete omission of major plot points and character arcs from the source material. This fundamentally breaks the adaptation requirement. While some individual action lines are directible, the overall structure is disjointed and lacks dramatic pacing due to the missing content. Dialogue is minimal and often invented or generic, failing to capture the book's voice. This draft is not production-ready as it does not faithfully adapt the source.
gemini-2.5-flash.gemini-2.5-flash: Screenplay B is an exceptionally faithful adaptation, covering virtually all major narrative beats and preserving authentic dialogue directly from the source. Character introductions are clear, consistent, and provide good visual detail for casting. AI video directibility is very strong, with action lines describing concrete, camera-observable actions suitable for short clips. The pacing effectively mirrors the book's dramatic arc, and sound design cues are well-integrated. This screenplay is highly production-ready.
gemini-2.5-flash.grok-4.5: Screenplay C demonstrates excellent adaptation fidelity, covering all major plot points and retaining authentic dialogue. Character disambiguation is strong, with specific visual details for key figures, and the 'identity locked' note is a valuable production instruction. AI video directibility is very good, though a few action lines contain minor internal states or combine slightly too many actions for a single, strict 5-10 second clip, requiring minimal refinement. Pacing, dialogue authenticity, and sound design are all expertly handled. This screenplay is production-ready.
gemini-2.5-flash.claude-sonnet-5: Screenplay D offers a highly faithful and comprehensive adaptation of the source material, including nearly all major beats and authentic dialogue. Character descriptions are specific and consistent, aiding casting clarity. AI video directibility is strong, but a noticeable number of action lines include internal states or motivations (e.g., 'trustingly,' 'nursing his wrath,' 'ablaze with the joy'), which would require rephrasing for strict camera-observable actions. The dramatic pacing and sound design are excellent, effectively conveying the narrative's progression. This screenplay is production-ready with minor revisions needed for directibility.
gemini-2.5-flash.grok-4: Screenplay E provides excellent adaptation fidelity and authentic dialogue, covering the source material thoroughly. Character disambiguation is generally strong, though some minor characters lack specific visual detail. However, its AI video directibility is significantly hampered by a very high frequency of internal states, emotions, and motivations embedded within action lines (e.g., 'nursing his wrath,' 'panic rising,' 'sensing kindness'). These would require substantial rephrasing to be strictly camera-observable actions for AI generation. Dramatic pacing and sound design are well-executed. This screenplay is production-ready but requires considerable revision on directibility.
gemini-2.5-flash.gpt-4o-mini: Screenplay F suffers from a severe penalty in adaptation fidelity due to significant simplification and condensation of major plot points in the latter half of the book, losing critical detail and dramatic impact. Character descriptions are sparse and inconsistent. AI video directibility is poor, with an overwhelming number of action lines describing internal states rather than observable actions. While the initial pacing is acceptable, the latter half feels rushed and generic. Dialogue authenticity also declines in the condensed sections. This screenplay is not production-ready due to its unfaithful adaptation and poor directibility.

JudgeSummaries.gpt-4o-mini: Strongest: Screenplay B because it excels in adaptation fidelity and dialogue authenticity, providing a strong narrative flow. Weakest: Screenplay C because it has pacing issues and inconsistent character descriptions that hinder its production readiness.
JudgeSummaries.o3-mini: Strongest: Screenplay F because it blends high fidelity, strong character clarity, and powerful dramatic and directible scenes ideal for AI video clips. Weakest: Screenplay E because its pacing and dialogue lack the dynamic impact and cinematic sharpness of the other candidates.
JudgeSummaries.grok-4.5: Strongest: Screenplay A because it uniquely balances exhaustive source fidelity, locked casting visuals and clip-scale concrete action. Weakest: Screenplay D because it invents characters and discards nearly the entire novel, making it unusable.
JudgeSummaries.grok-4: Strongest: Screenplay F because it delivers the most precise, filmable short-clip action lines while preserving every major source beat with locked character visuals. Weakest: Screenplay C because it collapses the entire narrative into generic narration, invents events, and drops nearly all characters and key conflicts.
JudgeSummaries.claude-sonnet-5: Strongest: Screenplay C, because it combines the most complete and accurate beat-for-beat coverage of the novel with clean, mostly single-action scene headings and a locked-identity note for consistent AI casting. Weakest: Screenplay D, because it replaces core named characters with invented ones, drops nearly the entire middle of the book (Spitz rivalry, Hal/Mercedes ordeal, the wager, the moose hunt, the Yeehat massacre), and ends on an unearned, truncated note, making it unusable as a faithful shootable draft.
JudgeSummaries.gemini-2.5-flash: Strongest: Screenplay B because it demonstrates exceptional fidelity to the source material, provides clear character disambiguation, and maintains strong AI video directibility with precise action lines and sound cues. Weakest: Screenplay A because it invents named characters and omits massive, critical plot arcs and character developments, rendering it an unfaithful and unusable adaptation of the source book.
